Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

on top of preposition

also on top, onto

classical

Caes. BC 2.10: super laterēs coria indūcuntur (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 21.35.12: aliīque super aliōs

super

preposition with the accusative

on top of, onto, over

The accusative serves for lying on top and for putting on top alike; poets also use the ablative. For plain “on”, Latin says in with the ablative: in mēnsā.

Other words

  • summus, summa, summum — the top of

    adjective: the top of … · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 1.48: in summā columnā (Lewis & Short, s.v. superus); Caes. BG 1.22: summus mōns (Lewis & Short); Traupman 396

    Latin names the top as part of the thing: in summā columnā, on top of the column.

  • īnsuper — on top, above

    adverb · also used · classical · Caes. BG 4.17: īnsuper bipedālibus trabibus immissīs (Lewis & Short); Cato, Agr. 76

Examples

  • aliīque super aliōs et jūmenta in hominēs occiderent

    and they fell on top of one another, and the pack animals onto the menLiv. 21.35.12

  • testō caldō operītō, prūnā īnsuper et circum operītō

    cover it with a hot lid, and with embers on top and all roundCato, Agr. 76

See also above, under, top.

SourcesLewis & Short: super · Lewis & Short: superus · Lewis & Short: insuper
